runs.name: ClearSign Technologies Corporation
runs.entry: Price **$3.21** (close 2026-10-09, aggregator, flagged) x **6,807,455 shares** (one class; the 10-Q cover, 0001104659-26-096539, checked against 6,307,455 issued at 2026-06-30 plus 500,000 sold to Otter Capital on 2026-07-21, 8-K 0001104659-26-086099) = cap **$21.85M**; net cash $11.64M; sovereign **5.60%** (UST 30Y, 2026-10-09). Primary document the FY2025 10-K (0001104659-26-037699, filed 2026-03-31); FY2025 operating cash $(4,736)k cross-checked to the filed cash-flow statement. Former name ClearSign Combustion Corp (to 2019); 1-for-10 reverse split 2026-03-16 (8-K 0001104659-26-025867); public offering at $4.33 (8-K 0001104659-26-068614); an at-the-market programme of up to $6.875M recommenced 2026-07-06. **Q1 OUT, a start-up by its economics on its own filing**: an operating loss every year read since FY2011, accumulated deficit $108.0M at 2026-06-30, about $105.3M of equity raised gross through 2025, the MD&A's own "an early stage, publicly traded technology company", the filer's own "cannot predict the rate of adoption" and "may never be profitable"; ruled out by name, **[L2007-015]**, **[M2008-088]**, with the ten-year economics unforeseeable, **[M2000-037]**, **[M2000-105]**. The analyst confesses as a CONVENTION of this run that start-up is read by economics, not age, and sets down TOO HARD (NATURE) as the reading if it were read by age; not TOO HARD (WORK), the deciding fact being adoption the filer says it cannot predict. Integrity facts recorded, not judged: an SEC inquiry into trading in the stock in 2020 (subject and status not in the filings); a 2025 board contest settled by cooperation agreements; three former directors suing in Delaware for advancement of legal fees (Case 2026-0082-CDW). Q2 to Q12 not reached. Beneath the stop, COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: owner cash (operating cash less stock pay in three forms, fixed capex and patent spending) negative every year FY2021-FY2025, mean $(6.14)M before interest, $(5.87)M after; no-growth case alone: range $(14.40) a share all-equity ($(15.40) equity-only), fair $(7.31) all-equity ($(8.62) equity-only), net cash $1.71 a share. Balance sheets 2016 to June 2026: almost all cash, refilled by share sales and drained by losses, no debt, no goodwill, shares up about 5.2 times pre-split, warranty liability $1.11M after twenty California refinery burners met emission limits only up to 80% of the specified firing rate. Customer concentration: three customers 81% of FY2025 revenue of $5.2M. Competitors named by the 10-K: Honeywell (Callidus, Eclipse, Maxon), GE and Linde file; John Zink (Koch), Zeeco (also its sole process-burner subcontractor), Haldor Topsoe, Hitachi, Fives, Cleaver Brooks and Power Flame do not; not compared, Q2 not reached. Citations: the analyst's check 23 ids, 17 fragments clean; the dispatcher's script (`fold_cite_check.py`) 23 ids present, 14 fragments, 0 slips. check_framework PASS. Analyst's gaps for the operator: (1) start-up is not defined in the text (age or economics); (2) Q7 has no rule for a cash stream negative every year; (3) the fair-price definition assumes a positive range, so a negative fair price gives the alert nothing to arm; (4) not obtained: the rivals' filings, press releases, the earnings-call transcript; FY2016-FY2020 cash flows from XBRL, not the filed documents.
runs.narr: Q1 OUT, a start-up by its economics: an 18-year-old maker of low-NOx burner technology that has never covered its costs, funded by share sales every year, three customers 81% of revenue, adoption the filer says it cannot predict. Beneath the stop owner cash is negative every year; range $(14.40) and fair $(7.31) all-equity against $3.21. Gaps reported: start-up undefined; Q7 silent on an always-negative cash stream.
